findings.location: Methods, Diagnostic prediction model (p.5) vs code/GC-diagnosis-model/run.ipynb cell 6 output: test, normal-patients (array([0., 1.]), array([94, 48])) = 142 rows
findings.evidence: The paper reports 'n test set (Cohort 1)' = 152 participants (Methods, Diagnostic prediction model (p.5)); the authors' own stored output (code/GC-diagnosis-model/run.ipynb cell 6 output: test, normal-patients (array([0., 1.]), array([94, 48])) = 142 rows) gives 142. Our re-run gives 142, which matches the stored output.

The paper reports "95% confidence" intervals, but the code computes the interval with 5%/95% bounds (`confidence_lower = sorted_scores[int(0.05 * len(sorted_scores))]`) (and 1 similar line(s)), which is a 90% interval; no 2.5%/97.5% bounds appear anywhere in the code. Check whether the reported intervals are 90% intervals.

Re-computed 'specificity 10-DM test set 1' = 0.9362 proportion does not match reported 0.926 proportion (Results p.3); relative difference 1.1%. Source: bp_work/data/GC-diagnosis-model/GC-diagnosis-model-pred-score-for-test.xlsx (our recount, TN=88,FP=6). Small gap: may be run-to-run variation (e.g. an unseeded random forest) or rounding; re-run with several seeds and pass the spread as `range`. No stored output from the authors was recorded for this value; it has not passed the reproduction gate, so it stays yellow. Check that the denominator, subset and filters match the paper's before asking the authors.

3 files whose names describe different data (external+test / test) have identical content (142 rows x 150 columns): data/GC-diagnosis-model/GC-diagnosis-model-pred-score-for-test.xlsx, results/GC-diagnosis-model/GC-diagnosis-model-pred-score-for-external-test.xlsx, results/GC-diagnosis-model/GC-diagnosis-model-pred-score-for-test.xlsx. One of them is the wrong file. Same pattern at 1 more place(s): run.ipynb code cell 14 line 9.

Hyper-parameter scan (deep_checks.py): the paper says "We set the coefficient of the L1 constraint as 0.01 and selected ten features with nonzero coefficients based on the misclassification error averaged from 10,000 times of random cross-validation." (l1 = 0.01); the code sets `alpha=0.005` at code/GC-diagnosis-model/run.ipynb:94 (l1 = 0.005). Same parameter, different value.

data/GC-diagnosis-model/discovery_set.xlsx (426 rows) contains 142 of the 142 rows of data/GC-diagnosis-model/Xtest.xlsx (also in 3 other test-named file(s): data/GC-diagnosis-model/GC-diagnosis-model-pred-score-for-test.xlsx, results/GC-diagnosis-model/GC-diagnosis-model-pred-score-for-test.xlsx, results/GC-diagnosis-model/GC-diagnosis-model-pred-score-for-external-test.xlsx); compared on 148 shared columns. If data/GC-diagnosis-model/discovery_set.xlsx was used for feature selection, tuning or preprocessing, the test samples took part in it. Check which file each step of the code reads.

perm.fit(Xtest, ...) fits on test-named data. If the result feeds feature selection, tuning or the final model, the test set is no longer independent. Same pattern at 2 more place(s): run.ipynb code cell 13 line 2; run.ipynb code cell 9 line 5.
Claim 'The 10-DM model discriminates GC from NGC in the external test set (Cohort 2) with AUROC above 0.85' holds in 75% of 40 universes. Single changes that flip it: alpha=0.01.
